question: Sofia's craft business starts the month with $222 in the register. A large custom order adds $73 to the till, which comes out to 7,300 cents. A viral social media post brings the register's total to 5 times what it had been. The business then pays out $1,023 in supply costs and shipping fees. A holiday rush brings the register's total to 8 times what it had grown to. Her business partner Ana, who handles a separate pop-up stand, brings in about $600 for comparison. A dozen candles were given away as free samples that month, though that number has nothing to do with the register total. How much money is in the register now?

In the morning, Carlos has 158 pages left to read for a school project. By midday, he manages to read through 61 of those pages. In the afternoon, his teacher extends the assignment and adds 49 more pages to the reading list. Later that afternoon, a bonus discussion guide adds 7 more pages to complete. By evening, the teacher tacks on 60 additional pages covering a related short story. His classmate Priya, who is reading a different book entirely, has 120 pages assigned for comparison. How many pages does Carlos have left to read now?

Lena starts a lemonade stand fundraiser with 50 dollars in her cash box. A busy Saturday morning adds another 50 dollars to the box. A local business sponsorship brings the total to 5 times what it had been. A matching donation from her school brings the box's total to 2 times what it had grown to. A viral fundraiser post brings the total to 9 times what it had been. At the end of the event, Lena splits the money evenly into 2 shares to donate to two different charities, and the story follows just one share from here. Her friend Marcus, running a bake sale nearby, raised about $300 for comparison. How much money is in Lena's share now?

In the morning, a charity bake sale starts with 192 cupcakes baked overnight. By midmorning, a second batch adds 52 more cupcakes to the table. In the afternoon, a local bakery donates 72 additional cupcakes, which comes out to roughly 18 pounds of extra treats. A volunteer mentions that 300 people attended last year's event, though that number has nothing to do with today's cupcake count. Later that afternoon, a mix-up in the kitchen ruins 49 cupcakes that have to be thrown out. By evening, a final rush of orders brings the remaining cupcakes to 5 times what they had been. How many cupcakes does the bake sale have now?

A distribution center starts the day with 227 pallets of goods in the yard. A morning shipment brings the pallet count to 9 times what it had been. A local supplier drops off 28 more pallets shortly after. A regional surge in orders brings the total to 3 times what it had grown to. The yard supervisor mentions that the facility employs about 85 workers, though that number has nothing to do with the pallet count. An emergency restock adds 50 more pallets to the yard. A massive outbound shipment finally ships out 3,440 pallets to retail stores across the region. How many pallets does the distribution center have in its yard now?

A candy shop starts the day with 232 lollipops on display. A school field trip buys up 116 of them within the first hour. A birthday party order then takes another 60 lollipops off the shelf. A clumsy display mishap costs the shop 24 more lollipops that shatter and can't be sold. At closing, the shop owner sets aside half of what remains for tomorrow's display, and the story follows only that half from here. A morning delivery the next day adds 32 more lollipops to that batch. How many lollipops does that batch have now?

Nadia's sticker collection starts the summer with 213 stickers in her binder. A trip to the craft store adds 28 more stickers. A trade with her cousin brings in 32 additional stickers. A sticker-swap event with her whole class brings her collection to 8 times what it had been. Her friend Bella, who just started collecting, has about 90 stickers for comparison. A final haul from a school fair brings Nadia's collection to 9 times what it had grown to. A dozen glitter pens were given out as prizes that day, though that number has nothing to do with the sticker count. How many stickers does Nadia have now?

A toy drive starts the season with 156 donated toys collected at the community center. A local business adds 10 more toys the next day. A school fundraiser contributes another 58 toys. A church group then donates 44 additional toys. A radio station's charity drive adds 54 more toys to the pile. A dozen wrapping paper rolls were also dropped off, though that has nothing to do with the toy count. A final weekend donation event brings in 26 more toys. How many toys does the community center have now?

A recycling center starts the month with 119 pounds of aluminum cans collected. A neighborhood drive adds 27 more pounds. A school competition contributes another 74 pounds, which comes out to about 34 kilograms. A citywide collection event brings the total to 3 times what it had been. A record-breaking corporate donation brings the stockpile to 4 times what it had grown to. A final weekend drop-off adds 69 more pounds. How many pounds of aluminum does the recycling center have now?

Aisha's penny jar starts the year with 126 pennies in it, which comes out to $1.26. A summer of chore money adds 25 more pennies. A yard sale brings the jar's total to 3 times what it had been. A birthday gift adds 45 more pennies to the jar. A final holiday bonus from her grandparents brings the jar to 6 times what it had grown to. Her brother Sam, who saves nickels instead, has about 200 coins for comparison. How many pennies does Aisha's jar have now?

A theater's ticket counter starts opening night with 235 tickets pre-sold. A last-minute rush brings the count to 3 times what it had been. A group discount promotion then brings the total to 7 times what it had grown to. A walk-up sale adds 66 more tickets. Another wave of walk-ups adds 21 more. A final flurry right before curtain adds 22 more tickets. A block of 3,737 tickets is then released back to a partner venue as part of a co-hosting deal. How many tickets does the theater have now?

In the morning, a food bank starts the day with 92 crates of produce in storage. By midmorning, a farm donation brings the total to 8 times what it had been. At midday, a grocery store adds 50 more crates. In the afternoon, a second grocery chain contributes 54 more crates. By late afternoon, a community garden adds another 53 crates. In the evening, a large distribution event sends out 571 crates to local shelters. Right before closing, a final rescue shipment brings the remaining crates to 5 times what they had been. The volunteer coordinator, Wendy, mentions that her counterpart at a sister food bank, Marcus, manages about 400 crates for comparison. How many crates does the food bank have now?

In the morning, Jordan has 111 comic books stacked in his closet. By midday, a garage sale find brings his collection to 2 times what it had been. In the afternoon, a big trade at a comic convention brings his total to 4 times what it had grown to. His friend Kai mentions that the convention had over 3,000 attendees, though that number has nothing to do with his comic count. By evening, Jordan sells 456 comics to a dealer to make room on his shelves. Right before bed, he splits his remaining comics evenly into 3 boxes to store in the attic, and the story follows just one box from here. Kai, who has a much smaller collection, owns about 60 comics for comparison. How many comics does that box have now?

Ravi's baseball card binder starts the trading season with 176 cards, which comes out to nearly 4 pounds of cardstock if you weighed the whole binder. A big trade at school adds 18 more cards. A card show haul brings his total to 5 times what it had been. A lucky pack pull brings his collection to 3 times what it had grown to. A trade with his neighbor adds 20 more cards. A final gift from his uncle adds 57 more cards. His friend Deepak, who just started collecting, has about 150 cards for comparison. How many cards does Ravi have now?

In the morning, a bookstore starts inventory day with 134 paperbacks on the clearance table. By midmorning, a returned box adds 11 more paperbacks. At midday, a bulk donation brings the total to 7 times what it had been. In the afternoon, a library sale contributes 30 more paperbacks. A dozen bookmarks were tucked into random copies that morning, though that number has nothing to do with the book count. By evening, a huge clearance rush sells off 961 paperbacks. Right before closing, a final donation brings the remaining stack to 6 times what it had been. Overnight, a restocking crew brings the table's total to 4 times what it had grown to. How many paperbacks are on the clearance table now?

A puzzle club starts a tournament with 30 puzzle pieces scattered across the table for a warm-up round. The pieces are split evenly into 6 trays for the six teams competing, and the story follows just one team's tray from here. A bonus round adds 8 more pieces to that tray. A speed challenge adds 27 more pieces. The club mentions that 45 people signed up to watch the tournament, though that number has nothing to do with the piece count. A final mega-round brings the tray's total to 6 times what it had been. A scoring penalty then removes 101 pieces from the tray for a rules violation. How many pieces does that tray have now?

In the morning, Leah has 66 seashells in her collection from a previous trip to the coast. By midday, she finds 3 more shells during a beach walk. In the afternoon, her family stops at a second beach and she adds 18 more shells to her bag. By evening, a friend gives her a whole jar of shells, bringing her collection to 4 times what it had grown to. Right before bed, she sorts through a box from her grandmother's attic, bringing her total to 5 times what it had been. Her cousin Nora, who collects sea glass instead, has about 40 pieces for comparison. How many seashells does Leah have now?

A quilting circle starts the project with 163 fabric squares cut and ready. A big quilt for a charity auction uses up 125 of those squares. A second smaller project uses another 22 squares. A mistake in cutting wastes 5 more squares. A fabric store donation adds 36 more squares to the pile. A dozen spools of thread were also donated that day, though that number has nothing to do with the square count. A final contribution from a member's stash adds 13 more squares. How many fabric squares does the quilting circle have now?

A concert promoter starts pre-sales with 133 tickets already sold, which comes out to just over $6,650 in early ticket revenue. A radio campaign brings sales to 8 times what they had been. A social media blitz brings sales to 5 times what they had grown to. The promoter splits the sold tickets evenly into 5 batches for different box offices, and the story follows just one batch from here. A last-minute surge brings that batch's total to 6 times what it had been. A refund wave for a scheduling conflict removes 2,593 tickets from the batch. A final cancellation policy removes another 2,252 tickets. How many tickets does that batch have now?

In the morning, a farmer's roadside stand has 209 ears of corn stacked up, worth roughly 20,900 cents if you priced them all individually. By midday, a bus tour stopping by brings the stand's stock to 2 times what it was. In the early afternoon, 296 ears are sold to a nearby restaurant for a big event. The farmer's neighbor, Hank, mentions his own stand only sold 150 ears today, way less than this stand's activity. By late afternoon, the remaining corn is split evenly between the stand's two baskets, and the story follows just one basket from here. That evening, 17 more ears are added from a late harvest run. How many ears of corn are in that one basket now?

A toy drive collection box has 99 toys in it at the start of December, valued at roughly 9,900 cents in donated retail tags combined. A school assembly adds 24 more toys. A matching-donation event brings the box's count to 3 times what it was. A local business drops off 29 more toys. A final weekend donation drive brings the count to 3 times what it had grown to. On distribution day, 888 toys are given out to families in need. How many toys are left in the collection box?

A concert hall starts ticket sales with 237 seats reserved. A group booking adds 7 more seats. A huge presale event brings the reserved count to 6 times what it was. A processing error releases 1,322 of those reservations back into general inventory. A second presale wave brings the remaining reservations to 7 times what they were. The hall's manager, Yusuf, mentions a smaller venue down the street only reserved 300 seats today, far fewer than this hall. A late cancellation wave removes 436 reservations. The remaining reservations are then split evenly across 6 ticket windows, and the story follows just one window's count from here. How many reservations does that one window have?

Mateo has 63 dollars saved from chores. He spends 36 dollars on a new skateboard deck. He then spends 6 dollars on grip tape. He splits what's left evenly among 3 savings jars for different goals, and the story follows just one jar from here. His friend Cole, who's saving for the same skate park pass, mentions his own jar has 40 dollars, way more than what's in Mateo's jar right now. The corner shop, separately, restocked 500 candy bars that week, unrelated to Mateo's savings. That jar loses 1 more dollar to a vending machine mishap. A bonus from raking leaves brings that jar's total to 4 times what it had left. A final birthday gift adds 36 more dollars to the jar. How much money is in that jar now?

A school's rock collection display starts the semester with 20 rocks. A field trip haul brings the display's count to 6 times what it was. The rocks are then split evenly across 5 display cases, and the story follows just one case's rocks from here. The school's mineral collection down the hall, separately, has 200 specimens, unrelated to this display. That case then gains 33 more rocks from a student donation. A parent volunteer adds 3 more rocks found on a hike. A final addition of 4 rocks comes from a retiring teacher's old collection, weighing in at just under 2 kilograms combined, or about 4.4 pounds. How many rocks are in that one display case now?

A bicycle shop has 51 inner tubes in stock at the start of the week, worth about 5,100 cents combined at wholesale price. A weekend of repairs uses up 42 tubes. A new shipment adds 74 more tubes. A big back-to-school rush brings the stock to 7 times what it had grown to. The shop's neighboring café, separately, sold 600 cups of coffee that week, unrelated to the tube count. A second shipment adds 57 more tubes. A final holiday rush brings the stock to 9 times what it was. How many inner tubes does the shop have now?
